summary: Aristotle C. Dy works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London, where he studied under Antonello Palumbo (attested 2013).
Aritri Dutta is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. She pursued an external PhD at Leiden University under the doctoral supervision of Henk Blezer (attested 2026).

Arjo Vanderjagt, a philosopher and historian, studied at the University of Groningen (1971–1981). He held posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1976–1979), the University of Groningen (1994–2009), and Utrecht University (2007).

Indologist and linguist Arlo Griffiths studied at Harvard and Leiden (PhD 1999–2004) under Henk Bodewitz. He held posts at Leiden (attested 2002), Groningen (~2004–2005), the Kern Institute (~2005–2008), and became professor at the EFEO in 2008.

Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren was a historian and Indologist. After studying at the University of Göttingen (PhD 1779–1784) under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Ludwig Timotheus Spittler, he served as a lecturer and professor at Göttingen from 1784 onward.

Historian Arnold J. Toynbee studied at Winchester College and Balliol College, Oxford. He taught at King's College London (1919–1924) and subsequently served at the London School of Economics and as director of Chatham House (~1925–1955).

Arthur Anthony Macdonell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen, Oxford, Tübingen, and Leipzig. He was Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford from 1888, a fellow at Balliol from 1899, and vice president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1921–1924).

Indologist and linguist Arthur Berriedale Keith studied at Edinburgh under Julius Eggeling and at Balliol College, Oxford, under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He worked at the Colonial Office (~1901–1914) before serving as professor at Edinburgh from 1914 to 1944.

Indologist and linguist Arthur Coke Burnell studied at King's College London under Theodor Goldstücker, as well as under Michael Viggo Fausbøll and Heinrich August Jäschke. He served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1860 to 1880.

Arthur Emanuel Christensen was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and under Friedrich Carl Andreas, later holding the first chair of Oriental studies at Copenhagen from 1919 to 1945.
Arthur F. Buehler is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied under Annemarie Schimmel and held an academic post at Victoria University of Wellington.

Arthur F. Wright worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied at Stanford, Oxford, and Harvard under John King Fairbank. He taught at Stanford University from 1947 and became Charles Seymour Professor of History at Yale in 1959.

Philosopher Arthur Hilary Armstrong studied at Jesus College, Cambridge. He taught at Swansea, the University of Malta, Beaumont College, and Cardiff, before serving as Gladstone Professor of Greek at the University of Liverpool (1950–1972).
Arthur John Evans was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Harrow School and at Brasenose College, Oxford, beginning in 1870.

Indologist and historian Arthur Llewellyn Basham completed his BA and PhD at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett. He taught at SOAS (1948–1965), headed Asian Civilizations at the Australian National University (~1965–1978), and held visiting posts at Toronto and The Asiatic Society.

Arthur Philip McKeown specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2005), where he studied under Parimal G. Patil, Pelri Sanggye, and Diana L. Eck.

Arthur Schopenhauer was a philosopher who studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Jena. After studying under Friedrich Schleiermacher, August Boeckh, and Friedrich August Wolf, he lectured at the University of Berlin between 1820 and 1831.

Indologist Arthur Venis studied at Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford. He served as professor and principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1881 to 1888 and later taught post-Vedic Sanskrit at the University of Allahabad (~1914–1918).

Arthur Waley was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at King's College, Cambridge. He worked at the British Museum (1913–1929) and later served as an honorary lecturer in Chinese poetry at SOAS (1948).

Indologist Arthur William Ryder studied at Harvard, Berlin, and Leipzig, learning under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He taught Sanskrit at Harvard (1902–1906) and subsequently served as professor of Sanskrit at UC Berkeley (~1906–1938).
